promise: Increase South Africa's contribution pledge for the continental Ebola response to $13.5 million
description: Ramaphosa announced the increased pledge on June 16, 2026. He separately urged donors to convert pledges into cash, countermeasures or technical support; the pledge itself does not prove disbursement.
evidence: Pledge increased to $13.5 million announced June 16, 2026
Funding forms part of the African Union Ebola plan running June-November 2026

review.note: Primary speech confirms $13.5m pledge and date, but does not bind payment to November 30. Continental response-plan duration is not automatically South Africa's payment deadline. No actual transfer receipt found.

promise: Pursue a security crackdown on armed criminal groups rather than continue the prior peace-talks approach
description: De la Espriella outlined the policy in his August 7, 2026 inaugural address. The presidency announced termination of three dialogue processes on August 30; this is a policy action, not proof of eradicated crime.
evidence: Inaugural address pledges crackdown on armed groups and drug cartels
First-100-days focus on security expected, running to mid-November 2026

review.note: Inaugural hardline policy is supported; later government statement documents ending three dialogue processes. Analysts' first-100-days expectations cannot supply a presidential deadline or prove security outcomes.
